subject: Bridge renewal: rate ladder, commit uplift and incentive mechanics
messages:
From: Sara Malik <sara@edgescale.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Joe Grant <joe@edgescale.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal conversation: pricing hold & staggered uplift

Hi Marissa,

EdgeScale's renewal with Redwood is up on 2027-07-15 and our procurement team asked me to start the pricing conversation early so we can lock terms before Q3 forecasting. A few constraints on our side:

- We need a 12-month price hold for core generation calls (stable unit cost) to plan product-level budgets.
- We're prepared to increase our committed capacity (we currently have a 450k token/month commit) but want a clear ladder for discounts as we step up.
- To compensate timing, we'd like a one-time credit applied to Q3 invoices if we sign by June 15.

High-level ask: price hold + staged uplift. Rough trade we can consider: +20% commit in exchange for a 12% rate discount + $50k one-time credit. I'm attaching our usage summary for Q1/Q2.

Can you share what flexibility Redwood has on a short lock + credit structure? Also copying Joe (finance) who will be in the procurement call next week.

Thanks,
Sara Malik
Head of Platform Operations
EdgeScale

Attachment: usage_summary_q1q2.csv (stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Malik <sara@edgescale.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation: pricing hold & staggered uplift

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear ask and the timeline. Appreciate the early heads-up.

I've run the numbers with Ben and we can propose two feasible paths that balance budget predictability and Redwood's unit economics:

1) Accelerated-lock (fast sign by June 15)
   - 15% standard rate discount on your committed SKU
   - 15% increase to committed capacity (from 450k -> 517.5k tokens/mo)
   - $30,000 one-time invoice credit applied in Q3

2) Staggered ladder (preferred for growth planning)
   - 0% immediate discount on sign; price hold guaranteed for 9 months on current rates
   - Discount steps as commits hit 10% / 20% / 30% uplift thresholds: 6% / 10% / 14% respectively
   - $50,000 credit split across two milestones: $25k on signing, $25k when you hit 20% uplift
   - Clawback: credits prorated if actual usage remains below 70% of the committed rate after 12 months

I attached a quick rate_ladder_proposal.xlsx that shows invoice math for both options and monthly cashflow impact. Ben is copied — he can provide the amendment language and approvals path.

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-min call this week to walk procurement through the ladder and legal mechanics.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Principal Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachment: rate_ladder_proposal.xlsx (stub)

From: Sara Malik <sara@edgescale.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Joe Grant <joe@edgescale.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation: pricing hold & staggered uplift

Marissa — thanks, that helps. We reviewed both options internally. A few follow-ups from procurement and finance:

- The Accelerated-lock (option 1) is attractive for predictability but the 15% discount is below what our CFO expects given our growth runway. For a fast sign we'd need 18% + the $50k credit.
- For the Staggered ladder: we like the milestone structure but we need the initial price hold to be 12 months (you proposed 9). Can Redwood extend the hold to 12 months on the ladder approach?
- On credits: procurement will only accept a credit that is either non-recoverable (no clawback) or clearly tied to usage milestones. They're ok with a utilization clause but need the threshold at 60% not 70%.

I'm attaching our procurement_timeline.pdf so you can see the internal sign-off dates — we really need final terms in place before June 16 to make the July renewal budget.

If you can come back with a firm amendment we can approve, we can route to legal and DocuSign.

—Sara

Attachment: procurement_timeline.pdf (stub)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sara Malik <sara@edgescale.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 10:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation: pricing hold & staggered uplift

Hi Sara — looping Markus for approval on the concession structure.

Marissa and I spoke with Finance; here's a convergent suggestion that preserves Redwood economics while matching EdgeScale's procurement needs:

- Agreed commercial: 10% committed rate discount + 18% committed capacity uplift (450k -> 531k tokens/mo)
- Price hold: 12 months guaranteed on the agreed SKUs
- One-time credit: $40,000 applied across first two invoices (20k + 20k)
- Credit mechanics: credits are milestone-triggered. Clawback only if average monthly utilization < 60% of committed capacity across months 3-12; clawback prorated over remaining term.

I'm attaching a draft amendment (amendment_edgescale_v2.pdf) reflecting the above. If this is acceptable I can push to Legal and spin up a DocuSign envelope.

Markus — quick ask: can you sign-off on the 10% / 18% package? We're trading a larger commit uplift for a smaller credit vs EdgeScale's ask.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Strategic Sales

Attachment: amendment_edgescale_v2.pdf (stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Malik <sara@edgescale.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Renewal conversation: pricing hold & staggered uplift

Sara — thanks to you and Joe for being flexible and to Ben/Markus for the fast turnaround. Per our call today, summary and next steps:

Agreed commercial terms (summary):
- 10% off committed rate, applied to committed SKU line items
- 18% committed capacity uplift (450k -> 531k tokens/month)
- 12-month price hold from effective date of amendment
- One-time credit: $40,000 paid as two $20k invoice credits (applied to first two invoices after amendment takes effect)
- Credit clawback: triggered only if average monthly utilization < 60% of committed capacity measured across months 3-12; any clawback is pro-rated and applied as a credit reversal on the following billing cycle.

Operational next steps:
1) Ben to route amendment_edgescale_v2.pdf to Legal for final review and prepare DocuSign envelope (Ben)
2) EdgeScale to confirm signature party and billing contact (Sara / Joe)
3) Marissa to schedule a 30-min AM/finance kickoff to align reporting and thresholds (I'll send a calendar invite)

If this captures everything, we'll have Legal issue the final amendment and route for signature. Thanks everyone — appreciate the collaborative approach.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Principal Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
